  "scientific_question": "Does enrichment of morphologically small CA1 pyramidal neurons specifically near reactive astrocytes capture a cleaner localized memory-decline signal than the current absolute proximal size features?",
  "approach": "Assign cells to CA1 using annotation polygons, identify CA1 Pyramidal Neuron and Reactive Astrocyte labels, and compute pyramidal cell areas from centered contours. Define a donor-specific 'small pyramidal' threshold from the area distribution of all CA1 pyramidal neurons in that donor, then compute the biomarker as: fraction of small pyramidal neurons among reactive-astrocyte-proximal CA1 pyramidal neurons minus fraction of small pyramidal neurons among reactive-astrocyte-distal CA1 pyramidal neurons.",

  "notes": "Use CustomAnnotations polygons after dividing annotation coordinates by 16 before region assignment. Compute contour area after centering contours to avoid float32 cancellation. A KD-tree over CA1 reactive astrocyte centroids is sufficient for the 80 px proximity query. If proximal or distal CA1 pyramidal counts are very low, return NaN rather than an unstable fraction.",
  "rationale": "Recent wins have consistently come from sharpening the CA1 pyramidal/reactive astrocyte niche, and round 7 suggests the informative part of the pyramidal size distribution is the small-cell tail rather than simple niche abundance or encirclement. The right next test is therefore a within-CA1 contrast: ask whether small pyramidal neurons are selectively concentrated in the reactive-astrocyte-proximal compartment relative to the donor's own distal CA1 background. That is biologically interpretable, easy to audit, and could either add new localized-vulnerability signal or replace a weaker absolute area member."
